sentence: This project studies how cellular responses to environmental stress work, using live-cell imaging, single-molecule fluorescence, and proteomics.
This project tries to find out why cancer screening rates differ by race and ethnicity, looking at healthcare system, patient, and provider factors.
This project studies how fused oncoproteins are degraded in undifferentiated sarcomas, a type of human cancer.
This project studies how herpes simplex virus infection builds nuclear structures that gather ribosome parts and RNA, and how they relate to viral fitness.
This project studies how tumors and T cells compete for lipids carried by low-density lipoproteins, and how that affects response to immunotherapy.
This project builds nanoplatforms with peptides that target macrophages to deliver RNA therapeutics against pulmonary infections.
This project builds computer models that use medical images and clinical notes to help diagnose ophthalmic diseases.
This project studies how a histone variant controls placental senescence and genome organization, using a model of trophoblast development.
This project studies the transcriptional events that form neural crest and ectodermal placode cells at the neural plate border.
This project studies whether a molecular mechanism called N6-methyladenosine plays a causal role in Alzheimer’s disease.
This project builds online case studies that use real biomedical data to explain computational technologies.
This project studies how splicing shapes development of the midface, using an avian model of cleft primary palate.
This project coordinates cancer research and provides research resources to reduce the cancer burden.
This project studies what primary care physicians believe causes obesity and how adults with obesity view physicians who point to genetic explanations.
This project designs a system that uses ecological momentary assessment signals to detect suicide risk in primary health care.
This project studies how social, built, and environmental features of an area affect substance misuse, mental health, cardiometabolic health, and mortality.
This project uses single-molecule approaches to watch enzymes unwind and cut DNA, and to study how DNA gyrase enzymes wind up the genome.
This project provides mass spectrometry tools to measure small metabolites and trace metabolic pathways in cancer research studies.
This project studies how molecular imaging tests change the care of prostate cancer, and builds a decision model of the tradeoffs of imaging.
